text:
alex: Heads up — we're seeing a sudden ephemeral port blowup in us-west-2 from the edge fleet. ~12k TIME_WAIT sockets and a spike of `connect: cannot assign requested address` in sidecar logs. Model pulls returning 503s. Any quick wins?

maria: Looking at sidecar logs now. Repro on scale-up: burst of hydration requests -> new TCP connects -> immediate TIME_WAIT pile. Sample log: 
[sidecar] 2026-03-20T14:02:12Z connect error: errno 99, Cannot assign requested address

devon: Are we on single NAT GW per AZ still? What EIP counts do we have?

alex: 3 NAT GW EIPs/az right now. The problem is fanout from many short-lived connections (model registry, S3 pulls, metrics).

li: Short term: enable connection pooling and increase keepalive on sidecars to reduce new socket churn. Also consider `tcp_tw_reuse=1` to reclaim TIME_WAIT quicker.

devon: I can push a sidecar change: set HTTP connection pool and SO_KEEPALIVE. Will canary.

maria: I'm opening an infra ticket to add two additional NAT GW instances across AZs — should add headroom for ephemeral ports at the AWS layer. ETA ~30m.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-210 — egress ephemeral port exhaustion in us-west-2. Pager: li.

li: Rolling canary with sysctl tweak now. Early metrics show new connect rate down ~40% on canary pods.

devon: Patch for daemonset (canary 5%): sysctl + adapter changes. Sample config:
```
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=60
# python requests adapter example
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
adapter = HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=100, pool_maxsize=200)
session.mount("https://", adapter)
```

maria: Medium term: stand up a per-AZ egress-proxy (nginx with keepalive + upstream pooling) fronted by NLB to reduce origin fanout and reuse sockets. Also prepping temporary EIP pool.

alex: Good. Also evaluate prefixlist / source NAT pooling to give more unique src ports if needed. Test plan: ensure NAT+NLB path doesn't re-introduce half-close issues.

devon: Canary landed. Watching sidecar logs for `errno 99` and sockets metric.

li: Dashboard: https://prom.redwood.internal/d/egress/ephemeral-ports — watching.

maria: Infra has provisioned extra NAT GW capacity and associated EIPs; propagating now.

alex: Action items: (1) finish canary + monitor 15m, (2) confirm NAT capacity increase and EIP attach, (3) start design for egress-proxy + NLB. I'll update thread in 20m.

devon: :thumbsup:

li: Will follow up with a short runbook snippet for on-call to triage ephemeral port spikes.

alex: Thanks everyone — so far mitigation looks promising on canary. Keep reactions and short updates here.
